# AMD Physical AI Simulation Benchmarks and Long-Term Video Reproduction

This chapter transforms the simulation, policy evaluation, and multi-perspective video processing in the AMD AI DevMaster Physical AI project into a reusable learning path. The content covers Every Embodied, RoboCasa365, DexJoCo, DISCOVERSE, RoboWits, and Unitree G1 safety control, and provides a unified explanation of task protocols, AMD ROCm［AMD Open Compute Platform］ execution paths, result metrics, and video export methods.

This page is responsible for providing an overview and route selection. The download, environment, migration, training, evaluation, and video commands for each benchmark have been split into separate tutorials:

| --- | --- |

| Creative Problem Solving | [RoboWits: restricted data, ACT/Pi0/Pi0.5 and mutation [mutation conditions] evaluation](14-robowits-rocm-download-training-and-creative-task-evaluation.md) |

## 1. Start with two long-term success cases

Both of the following videos have undergone closed loop reasoning and simulation recording on the AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395. Click on the cover to watch the complete MP4 file that maintains the original action rhythm［Video File］.

| DexJoCo Two-armed Hangman | RoboCasa365 Long-distance Food Preparation Task |
| --- | --- |
| [![Video cover of DexJoCo two-armed Hangman](../../../16-专题组队学习/04-AMD-ROCm策略复刻专题/assets/competition_showcase/dexjoco_bimanual_hanoi_poster.jpg)](https://ethan-chen-plus.github.io/amd-physical-ai-showcase/assets/videos/dexjoco/recovery/bimanual-hanoi.mp4) | [![Video cover of RoboCasa365 long-distance food preparation](../../../16-专题组队学习/04-AMD-ROCm策略复刻专题/assets/competition_showcase/robocasa_pack_identical_lunches_poster.jpg)](https://ethan-chen-plus.github.io/amd-physical-ai-showcase/assets/videos/robocasa-recovery/pack-success.mp4) |
| Pi0.5 Multi-task checkpoint［checkpoint］, two-armed coordination for handling and stacking; synchronized recording from external and left/right wrist perspectives, 47.6 seconds. | GR00T N1.5 Multi-task checkpoint［checkpoint］, PandaOmron performing continuous operations in the kitchen; synchronized recording from four perspectives, 195 seconds. |

These two cases demonstrate two complementary types of capabilities: DexJoCo focuses on dual arms and dexterous manipulation, while RoboCasa365 focuses on long-time-series tasks in home environments. They share the same engineering criteria: policy outputs must truly advance the simulator, task success conditions must be determined by the environment, and videos must correspond exactly with the results recorded for that round.

## 2. Simulation and Policy Matrix

| System | Robots and Tasks | Policy or Controller | AMD Execution Content | Archived Results |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Every Embodied | MuJoCo cup grasping and stable placement | SmolVLA, Pi0, ACT | Data collection, training, closed loop evaluation, four-view video | SmolVLA achieved strict physical success `57/60`, red cup `27/30`, blue cup `30/30` |
| RoboCasa365 | PandaOmron kitchen manipulation, 16 fixed tasks | GR00T N1.5, Pi0.5 | PyTorch［tensor computing framework］ inference, 16×50 same protocol evaluation, four-view video | GR00T `230/800`; Pi0.5 `142/800` |
| DexJoCo | 11 dual-arm and dexterous tasks | Pi0.5 multi-task model | JAX［high-performance array computing framework］ native ROCm［AMD open computing platform］ inference, closed loop evaluation, three-view video | Official fixed seed［random seed］ is `5/11`; 10/11 tasks in the fixed seed［random seed］ archive have reproducible success cases |
| DISCOVERSE | AIRBOT, MMK2, expert trajectory and synthetic data | Expert state machine, ACT, etc. | Access control execution, task execution, data generation, three-channel 1080p video, 3DGS［three-dimensional Gaussian splashing］ rendering | Access control execution `18/18`; AIRBOT `12/12`; MMK2 `8/8`; high-definition tasks `4/4` |
| RoboWits | Manipulation tasks under unexpected conditions | ACT | W7900 training, checkpoint［checkpoint］ saving, inference and video evaluation | Complete training and evaluation toolchain, suitable for anomaly condition analysis |
| Unitree G1 | Full-body obstacle avoidance under ball-throwing threat | Predictive CBF［predictive control obstacle function］ | PyTorch［tensor computing framework］ predictor, fixed-round replay and safety metrics | Fixed seed［random seed］ `8/8`, minimum spacing `0.422 m` |

This matrix can be learned in three ways:

1. **Policy training route**: Use data from the controllable cup grasping task in Every Embodied, and conduct training with strict success evaluation.
2. **Multi-task evaluation route**: Learn about multi-task checkpoint loading, action interfaces, batch closed loop, and video indexing using RoboCasa365 and DexJoCo.
3. **Simulation engineering route**: Understand multi-robot access control operations, synthetic data, rendering, and safety control using DISCOVERSE, 3DGS［three-dimensional Gaussian splashing］, and Unitree G1.

## 3. Unified Reproduction Process

The commands for different simulators vary, but the reproduction process can be unified into six stages:

```text
固定上游版本与任务配置
        ↓
确认 AMD GPU［图形处理器］、ROCm［AMD 开放计算平台］和框架后端
        ↓
加载资产、机器人、相机与任务成功条件
        ↓
加载 checkpoint［检查点］、归一化统计和动作接口
        ↓
运行固定 seed［随机种子］闭环评估并保存逐回合结果
        ↓
导出多视角视频、汇总成功率和阶段指标
```

It is recommended to save the following minimum structure for each experiment:

```text
runs/{system}/{model}/{task}/
├── run_config.json
├── episodes/
│   ├── seed_000.json
│   └── seed_000.mp4
├── stats.json
└── videos/
```

`run_config.json` records tasks, models, cameras, control frequencies, and seeds; per-round JSON［structured data files］ record success conditions and stage status; `stats.json` aggregates from per-round files to avoid manual entry of success rates.

## 4. RoboCasa365: Home task evaluation with the same protocol

RoboCasa365 is used for a formal comparison with 16 tasks, and each task has 50 rounds. GR00T N1.5 and Pi0.5 use the same task directory, number of rounds, and success conditions, so they can be directly compared:

| Model | Number of Tasks | Number of Rounds | Number of Successes | Success Rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GR00T N1.5 | 16 | 800 | 230 | 28.75% |
| Pi0.5 | 16 | 800 | 142 | 17.75% |

RoboCasa365 uses four cameras for video: a third-person camera in the center, a third-person camera on the left, a third-person camera on the right, and a hand-eye camera. The four streams are combined at the same simulation moment, allowing for simultaneous observation of the overall path, arm posture, occlusion, and end contact.

The `PackIdenticalLunches` on the chapter homepage was successfully grasped using GR00T N1.5 in a successful round. It continuously demonstrated target recognition, approach, grasping, transportation, and placement, making it more suitable as a long-time sequence reproduction case than a single-step door opening and closing.

## 5. DexJoCo: Native ROCm JAX Multi-task Inference

DexJoCo’s 11 tasks share the official Pi0.5 multi-task checkpoint. The AMD running environment uses Python 3.12, ROCm 7.14.0, and JAX/JAXlib 0.10.0, and performs GPU matrix pre-checking, model loading, action generation, and simulator closed loop.

The official evaluation fixes the seed to 0, with 1 round for each task, and the result is `5/11`. Subsequently, only the tasks that fail are checked for seed 1–10 in sequence, and the process stops at the first successful round. This fixed profile enables reproduction of successful videos for 10/11 tasks. The two sets of data serve different purposes: the former is used for model comparison, while the latter is used to observe the task completion process and debug the action interface.

The video of the two-arm Hanoi tower uses three synchronized perspectives:

- External perspective: observing the coordination of both arms, the position of building blocks, and the final stacking;
- Left wrist perspective: observing the approach and grasping by the left hand;
- Right wrist perspective: observing the handling and placement by the right hand.

## 6. DISCOVERSE: Execution, Expert Data, and High-Resolution Rendering

DISCOVERSE migration connects the operation of access control, robot tasks, expert data, and videos into a complete chain:

- All 18 access control operations pass;
- 12 AIRBOT tasks and 8 MMK2 tasks have been verified for execution;
- Expert trajectories can be converted into training data;
- High-definition tasks export three-channel 1920×1080 camera footage simultaneously;
- 3DGS [three-dimensional Gaussian splashing] is used for scene rendering and dynamic playback.

The key interface here is not a single reasoning function, but rather a contract between the simulation state, camera, actions, success conditions, and data writing. It is recommended to first generate a complete trajectory using the expert state machine, then convert the observations and actions into the LeRobot data format, and finally integrate them with ACT, SmolVLA, or Pi0 series policies.

## 7. Every Embodied: From Training to Strict Physical Success

The Every Embodied cup-picking task is suitable as a learning entry point, as it is short in length, has clear success criteria, and the training cost is controllable. For the official results of SmolVLA, 30 fixed seeds for red cups and 30 for blue cups are used. Strict physical success requires completing lifting, transportation, placement, and stable maintenance, ultimately resulting in `57/60`.

The complete training and evaluation interfaces are split in this special topic:

## 8. Exporting Multi-Perspective Videos

Multi-view videos should be captured during the same simulation cycle, and all cameras share the same frame index. Here is the general structure:

```python
frames = {name: [] for name in camera_names}

for step in range(max_steps):
    action = policy.select_action(observation)
    observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)

    for camera_name in camera_names:
        frames[camera_name].append(env.render(camera_name=camera_name))

    if terminated or truncated:
        break
```

It is recommended to retain the following during export:

- Original video from a single camera, facilitating per-view diagnosis;
- Multi-view composite video, enabling quick review;
- Successful round posters, suitable for display in README［project description］ and the course homepage;
- Per-round JSON［structured data file］, linking the video with task results.

## 9. Learning Outcomes

After completing this chapter, it is recommended to prepare your own AMD simulation reproduction package:

| Output | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Environment records | AMD devices, ROCm［AMD Open Compute Platform］, PyTorch［Tensor computation framework］, or JAX［High-performance array computing framework］ versions |
| Task configuration | Robot, task, camera, control frequency, number of rounds, and seed［random seed］ |
| Model records | Checkpoint［checkpoint］ source, normalization statistics, and action interface |
| Results | Number of successes per task, total denominator, and stage metrics |
| Videos | At least one complete successful round and corresponding per-round JSON［structured data file］ |
| Review | Key adaptation points in the environment interface, model interface, and physical success conditions |
